mediaTips.category: FINDING THE RIGHT JOURNALIST OR PUBLICATION
mediaTips.title: Media Tips
mediaTips.hint: Use these tips to target your story effectively.
mediaTips.text:
LEADING WITH THE LOCAL STORY

When approaching local media, lead with the local story. Mention Amazon as the sponsor of the Tangible World Coding Cup, but do not make the sponsorship the main angle unless it is specifically relevant to the story. The focus should remain on your learners, your school and your community.

— — —

HOW TO FIND THE RIGHT JOURNALIST

1. LOCAL NEWSPAPERS
Search for your local paper and look for the Education Editor, Schools Reporter or Community News reporter. If there isn't a specialist, send to the news desk.

2. LOCAL RADIO
Many local and community radio stations run education or community segments. Search for your station's contact page and look for the news desk or a relevant programme.

3. EDUCATION PUBLICATIONS
Look for regional or national education publications and websites that cover school news. Teacher-focused outlets often welcome positive classroom stories.

4. COMMUNITY PUBLICATIONS
Parent magazines, community newsletters, faith community publications and local business news often welcome feel-good school stories.

WHAT MAKES A STRONG PITCH
— A local angle (your school, your town, your community)
— A real person: a learner or teacher who can be quoted or interviewed
— Good photographs (with consent in place)
— Timing: send your release shortly after the event while it is still fresh

TIPS
— Email is almost always better than a phone call for an initial approach
— Keep your pitch email short — three paragraphs maximum
— Follow up once after 2–3 days if you hear nothing
— Do not exaggerate or claim results that are not confirmed
